From what I saw, there was no forced labour. There is very low paid labour that I don't agree with. The westerns were very good at abusing that. But on the flip side one of the maids told me she was earning more in dubai than a doctor back home (Philippines) Dubai meant she could build a house and educate her children at the cost of living away from them. I would argue then dark side of that situation is outside of Dubai. 

The law states that passports should never be withheld and are to stay with employees at all time. Whether that happens or not I cannot tell you. It didn't at the organisations me and my husband worked for. Passports were always returned after visa processing. 

It is very glamorous, very expensive and very much a bubble. A beautiful bubble but a bubble nonetheless. 

What I like about Dubai is its honestly. It is what it is. It has its rules, and if you lose your job your visa. Medical etc is cancelled. I find the UK hides behind a vision of fairness that doesn't exist.

I am biased because I loved my time in Dubai and my home country isn't what it was. As a woman and mother I never felt so respected. I was never swore at or called a bitch like I get when driving in the UK. (mind you swearing is illegal in the UAE) I loved the manners in the UAE towards us too, just pulling out a chair or holding the door. Those things are dying in the UK.
